no_target_yet.statement:
Let $a>0$, $t\ge0$, and $j\ge1$ be an integer. Put
\[
 g_t(q)=1+q+tq^2,\qquad x_k(q)=(k+a)g_t(q)\quad(k\ge0).
\]
Then $(x_k)$ satisfies \eqref{eq:strong}, and
\begin{equation}
 E_x^{j+2,j+1,j}=H_x^{j+2,j+1,j}=C_{a,j}g_t^4,\qquad
 C_{a,j}=\frac{j(j+1)^2(j+2)(2a+j+2)(4a+j+3)}{48}>0.
\end{equation}
The coefficient sequences of these two polynomials are log-concave
if and only if $0\le t\le5/2$.
no_target_yet.title: Gy's triple-product inequalities: nonnegativity and counterexamples to coefficient log-concavity

no_target_yet.statement:
Fix real numbers $a>0$, $\varepsilon>0$ and $t\ge5/2$, and set
$x_k=(k+a)g_t+\varepsilon$ for $k\ge0$. These polynomials have
strictly positive coefficients, are pairwise coprime in $\mathbb R[q]$,
and satisfy \eqref{eq:strong}. For every integer $j\ge1$, the two
differences at $(n,p,j)=(j+2,j+1,j)$ are equal and have nonnegative
coefficients, but their first coefficient log-concavity determinant
is strictly negative.
no_target_yet.title: Gy's triple-product inequalities: nonnegativity and counterexamples to coefficient log-concavity

no_target_yet.statement:
For $1\le j\le p\le n$, if all $x_k$ have nonnegative coefficients
and satisfy \eqref{eq:strong}, then $E_x^{n,p,j}$ and $H_x^{n,p,j}$
have nonnegative coefficients. This applies Gy's stated implication
from Conjecture~4.1 to its $q$-analogue, Conjecture~5.1
\cite[\S5, p.~15]{gy}, with coefficientwise nonnegativity made explicit.
Gy proved Conjecture~4.1 in \cite[Theorem~1.2, p.~3]{gy-bijective}.
The specializations below give Conjecture~5.2 and the corresponding
type~B nonnegativity statement.
